Now, finally, I want to end this session with what I call the law of indirect effort. The law of indirect effort says that we achieve our goals re-involve-involve-involving other people more indirectly than directly. Rather than going after the things we want from others directly, we instead turn it around and we go after them indirectly.

First of all, it says that if you want to impress, if you want others to be impressed by you, then be impressed by them. If you want to have a friend, be a friend If you want to have others help you, then you help them. If you want to be happy, make others happy. If you want to feel good about yourself, make others feel good about themselves.

And finally, the most important of all rules in relationships, in sales or anywhere else, is to practice the golden rule. Treat others the way you'd like them to treat you. Make them feel good about themselves the way you'd like them to make you feel good about yourself, and you'll be successful not only in selling, but in everything you do and with everyone you meet.
